sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: The aim of this document is to describe the web service Profile Management in terms of “what is it” and “how to use it”.
The input and output format and the methods exposed by the web service are contained in ProfileManagement.wsdl attached to this document in paragraph “WSDL”.
The methods provided by the web service are described in the paragraph “Available methods”.
Each method has a specific paragraph dedicated. The structure is as follows:
1. Import/update of Company and Users Data

2. Request data format: describes the possible operations on company (CREATE, UPDATE, CREATE_REGONLY and so on), on classification (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE and so on), on sub-users (CREATE, UPDATE, ENABLE, DISABLE and so on) and data elements (CREATE). Then, it describes the structure of the request. The request is composed of sections and every section is composed of fields to be filled. This paragraph specifies which fields are mandatory depending on the operation you want to perform and those that can be omitted.
3. Request samples: includes some examples of import requests.
4. Behaviour: describes how the web service processes the data passed in input, in case of some particular processes.
5. Response data format: describes the structure of the web service response and contains the list of possible error codes.
6. Export of Company and Users Data

7. Condition Filters: describes which fields can be used to filter the records to be extracted on specific conditions. So, the use of a condition filter allows to decrease the number of records extracted.
Example:
1. Component Filters: describes which sections can be exported. The use of a component filter increments the number of sections in the response to every record exported.
Example:
1. Results pagination: describes how the results in response are paginated.
2. Export Response Data format: describes the structure of the response in terms of exported fields and sections.
3. Request samples: includes some examples of export requests.
4. Error codes: contains a list of possible error codes.
5. WSDL: in this paragraph is attached the ProfileManagement.wsdl from which the web service has been created and is to be used to generate the client.
6. Available methods: contains the list of the methods provided by the web service.
7. Additional technical information: describes specific scenarios with possible impacts on the web service response:
8. DoS attack protection
9. MTOM
10. Errors handling
11. Time and Time Zone: describes the offset between the datetime fields shown in the web service, and the same ones displayed in the JaggaerAdvantage User Interface.
12. Best Practices: provides best practices to follow when designing integrations:
13. Multiple calls to the web service

14. Data Types and UI Default Labels: describes the type of the fields and the corresponding label in English language in the platform with the aim to simplify the mapping between the fields visible in the platform and the fields used in the web service.

sections.title: Company identification strategy
paragraphs: Web service needs to identify a company to perform requested operation, even if operation is not related to “main” company data (but refer to Classification, User or Data Element).
That’s why the operation code in company import request structure accept an empty value and the underlying companyInfo element is mandatory.
If the “bravoId” attribute is provided, system looks for a company having such value.
If Web service is configured to use the “extUniqueCode” attribute as company identifier and the “bravoId” attribute is not provided, system looks for a company having such “extUniqueCode” value.
If this value is not provided, according to the fields that have been chosen to be unique for each company (company identification strategy), the following attributes are used:

rows:
userAlias: system checks for a company whose super user has provided login.
extUniqueCode: this field is used if no company has been found having a superUser with provided userAlias. If the case, system checks for a company having the external unique code and, if it is found, we assume web service has been called to change the login information of the super user and operation can proceed.
extCode: this field is used if no company has been found having a superUser with provided userAlias and having the provided extUniqueCode. If the case, system checks for a company having the external code and, if it is found, we assume web service has been called to change the login information of the super user and operation can proceed.
fiscalCode and/or vat fields are used
VAT Code inside the country company resides (expressed by the isoCountry attribute)
fiscalCode: this field is used if the value of isoCountry attribute is contained in the list of country that must be checked for uniqueness
euVat: this field is used if the value of isoCountry attribute is not contained in the list of country that must be checked for uniqueness, but the country is a member of European Union
dAndBCode: this field is used if the value of isoCountry attribute is not contained in the list of country that must be checked for uniqueness, but the country is not a member of European Union

sections.title: User Role identification strategy
paragraphs: The userRole field in the company request can be filled with the code or the name (in the current locale) of a user company role. If the value passed is a valid code, the web services uses it. Otherwise, it verifies if the value passed is a user company role name in the current locale. If it is a valid name, the web service takes the corresponding code, otherwise an error is returned.

sections.title: Sub User identification strategy
paragraphs: To identify the sub user, it is possible to fill the login field or the extCode field or the userId field.

If the userId field is provided, the system tries to identify the sub user by userId. If the user exists, the system can update its external code (if the extCode field is provided) and its login data (if the login field is provided). If the user doesn’t exist, the system returns an error.
When the userId field is not provided, the system tries to identify the user by the login field or the extCode field.
If the login field is provided, the system checks for a user with the provided login:
1. If the user exists, and the field extCode is provided, it is used to update the existing external code of the user.
2. If the user doesn’t exist, the system checks the extCode field:
3. If no extCode is provided the system returns an error.
4. If the extCode is provided and not exist user with this external code, the system returns an error.
5. If the extCode is provided and exists user with such external code, the system updates the login data of the user with the login provided.
If no login field is provided, one of the fields userId or extCode must be specified mandatorily to identify the user.

sections.title: Export of Company and Users Data
paragraphs: This service allows supplier data registered on the JaggaerAdvantage platform to be exported.
It is possible to execute the data extraction by setting two types of criteria:
1. Conditional Filters
2. Component Filters

The export of company information is available by means of 2 different web-service methods: “ExportProfiles” and “ExportProfilesPaged”. Both methods accept the same import and provide the same results but the second one supports also the results “pagination” feature offered by all the other JINT web-services.
For this reason, the “ExportProfiles” is deprecated and is now available only for backward compatibility. All new integrations (or upgrade to existing ones) must use the “ExportProfilesPaged” method.

sections.title: Condition Filters
paragraphs: Condition filters allow the identification of a subset of company profile with certain features (id, status). Include filters on data-elements values (eVM answers) and seller classification and qualification.

sections.title: MAIN Condition filters
paragraphs: Condition filters are also available server side as restrictive conditions. The filter conditions entered client side will be joined with the filter conditions configured server side.

It is possible to enable the component filters according to particular values of the condition filters server side. By this way, it is possible to configure different chains, everyone with different restrictive conditions and therefore with different subsets of component filters enabled.

For instance, based on the specific configuration set up for the single integration, will be possible to allow the webservice client to export only Suppliers with a specific “secondary status”, even if this filter is not set by the integration client.

sections.title: Results pagination
paragraphs: In order to better manage performances, webservices export responses are limited to a predefined number of items that are configured on a single integration basis (usually it is defaulted to 100 objects per webservice call).

In order to retrieve the full list of objects matching the provided filtering criteria the webservice client has to perform multiple calls, one for each “page”. For instance, if an export call retrieves 250 objects and the maximum is set to 100, the webservice client is required to perform 3 webservice calls, one for objects from 1 to 100, one for object from 101 to 200 and the last for the remaining 50 objects.

In order to get the proper subset of results the webservice client can set in the webservice call the parameter startAt (default is 1). Information about how many objects are matching the current export request and how many of them have been returned in the current response are given in the response parameters
1. totRecords: number of objects matching the export criteria
2. returnedRecords: number of objects returned in the current response
3. startAt: index of the first item (it should be exactly what provided in the same parameter of the export request)
In the example above (250 objects, pagination set to 100), the following 3 webservice requests/responses have to be executed to have the full list of matching objects

sections.title: DoS attack protection
paragraphs: In the event the webservice client exceeds a preconfigured number of webservice calls per minute (usually 100), when this scenario was not previously agreed, the webservice could return an HTTP status 429 (Too Many Requests) as per RFC 6585 (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6585#page-3).
The response will also include the “Retry-After” header indicating how long the client has to wait before making a new request.

sections.title: MTOM
paragraphs: Since JINT allows to transfer attachments via webservices, all JINT webservices implements “Message Transmission Optimization Mechanism” (MTOM) over Soap 1.1.
Details are given in the following W3C specification http://www.w3.org/Submission/soap11mtom10.

sections.title: Errors handling
paragraphs: The web service has been designed to manage validation errors related to the SOAP Request content by including error code and error details in the SOAP Response. Possible error codes for each operation are listed in the specific tables in the previous "Error codes" chapters. These errors are not raised at protocol level. This design choice allows errors handling to any legacy system.
The table below describes how the web service responds:

SOAP Request is fully compliant to WSDL/SOAP protocol and the content is successfully processed by Jaggaer
SOAP Response with a success code
SOAP Request is fully compliant to WSDL/SOAP protocol but the content is not validated in the Jaggaer specific scenario (e.g. wrong object identifier)

sections.title: Time and Time Zone
paragraphs: The web service exports all fields of type datetime in the installation reference timezone, usually UTC (Universal Time Coordinated) that corresponds to timezone GMT (Greenwich Mean Time). This is evidenced by the date format, for example 2016-03-01T15:30:00.000+00:00, where +00:00 indicates that the offset from UTC is 0.
On the contrary, in the Jaggaer Advantage User Interface, datetime fields are displayed in the local time of the logged user, i.e. with the timezone associated to the given user.
So, it is possible to experience a time difference (offset) between a datetime field displayed in the Jaggaer Advantage User Interface and the same one exported by the web service.
For example, a user with CET timezone in the platform will see the dates shifted of 1 or 2 hours (depending on daylight saving time) compared to those exported by the web service in UTC.
The filter condition lastUpdateTime needs to specify the timezone in which the date is expressed, for example 2016-03-01 15:30:00.000 +0100 where +0100 indicates UTC+1.

sections.title: Multiple calls to the web service
paragraphs: We strongly recommend performing sequential calls.
In case of parallel calls, the web service put the requests in a queue and doesn't satisfy a request until the previous one has been completed.
Each request not satisfied after some time (default is 1 minute) is discharged and an error is returned (-998, Unable to acquire lock).

A high number of parallel calls may activate the protection mechanism against DoS attacks and the client may not be able to make further calls [see "DoS attack protection" in "4.4 Additional technical information"].
